Ziyu Acoustics began publishing on July 7, 2019. As of today, December 31, 2019, it has been running for almost six months and has published 21 articles, in three main categories: popular acoustics, the history of acoustics, and acoustics as a field of study.

As of today we have 1,750 followers: 1,346 men and 403 women, and we have also managed to attract one follower of unknown gender.

Our followers are spread across all of China’s major cities and a number of other countries. Apart from Qinghai and Tibet, where nobody follows us, every province in China has followers, with Guangdong, Beijing and Jiangsu in the top three.

The biggest turning point of our first six months came on October 25, when the account gained another powerhouse writer: Er Mu. With him on board, the account is run far more professionally. After some discussion, we settled on one article every two weeks, which leaves our day jobs untouched while keeping the quality as high as we can. Every article is revised many times between the first idea and publication. Structure and scientific rigor, choice of illustrations and layout, logic and wording all go through round after round of polishing, so that we keep the quality up while making sure the science we share is accurate and rigorous: responsible to our readers, and to ourselves. The price: weekend after weekend spent on the phone with Er Mu, over and over again…

My popular-science writing, and my life as a content creator, officially began around Christmas a year ago, when I started posting articles and answering questions on Zhihu every now and then. I started out of interest in acoustics and a slight fondness for playing the teacher, and I enjoy the satisfaction, and the small dose of vanity, that comes with spreading knowledge. There were times this year when I lacked the motivation to keep going, but most of the time I enjoyed the process. Every article takes a lot of time and effort to plan, research and write, but seeing what I write reach so many people, and help some of them, makes it well worth it. A year on, I’m as motivated as I was a year ago.

Through researching and writing this year, I’ve not only spread knowledge but also learned a great deal outside my own specialty, met many excellent fellow acousticians, and gained more chances to exchange ideas and hear about what’s going on. Er Mu and I run the account as a real venture. We’ve found out how hard it is to do something well, and we keep learning and finding our way, and getting something out of it.

The second decade of the 21st century is over; 2020 is about to arrive, and with it the next decade. It should be the most important decade of my life. I hope this account will stay with me through it and win even more followers in 2020.

In the new year we’ll keep up our pace of one article every two weeks, so 2020 will bring 24 more. Our focus remains popular acoustics, with pieces closer to everyday life as well as more specialized ones on particular topics.

I hope we reach five figures in followers. It doesn’t look very realistic, but a guy’s gotta have hope.

I hope to have more conversations with fellow acousticians and with anyone interested in acoustics.

And I hope you’ll leave lots of comments telling us what you’d like to know about acoustics. Each of us has only so much knowledge and so many ideas, and a single comment from you may well become the topic of our next article.

— Fanyu

At 9:45 pm I got a message from Fanyu: he’d written a year-end review and outlook for the account, could I take a look and see whether I wanted to add anything? He was planning to publish it at 10:00 pm.

Me: …

Me: We started the account because we wanted to do something for public science and promote this niche discipline. We hope what we write brings people some knowledge and inspiration, and sparks more interaction and discussion. Writing isn’t easy. I hope we can keep it up, so that for the 2020 review I’ll have a bit more time to write this paragraph.

— Er Mu

Finally, Happy New Year to you all! In 2020, may your careers flourish, and may you stay healthy and happy!
